check.description: Run the check after the agent finishes

targets.name: git
targets.note: Git 2.54+ runs config-based hooks (hook.<name>). Skillshare writes its own included file and helper scripts. Git reads configuration on every command; management never executes hooks.

targets.name: claude
targets.note: Claude Code runs settings.json hooks only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted; /hooks lists them read-only.

targets.name: codex
targets.note: Codex loads hooks.json together with inline [hooks] in config.toml, which Skillshare leaves untouched and lists as an additional source. Review and trust each new or changed hook in /hooks; project hooks load only when the project's .codex folder is trusted.

targets.name: gemini
targets.note: Gemini CLI reads hooks from settings.json. Project hooks are fingerprinted and warn until trusted again after any change; manage them with /hooks panel.

targets.name: copilot
targets.note: GitHub Copilot loads every JSON file in its hooks folder (COPILOT_HOME/hooks, or .github/hooks in a project, which loads only in a trusted folder). Skillshare writes one skillshare-<entry>.json per hook.

targets.name: cursor
targets.note: Cursor reads hooks.json (version 1, lowerCamelCase events) and reloads it when it changes; project hooks need a trusted workspace.

targets.name: droid
targets.note: Factory Droid reads hooks.json, and settings.json hooks only while hooks.json is absent, so Skillshare never creates hooks.json over inline hooks. Droid snapshots hooks at startup; review changes in /hooks.

targets.name: qwen
targets.note: Qwen Code reads hooks from settings.json; project hooks load only in trusted folders. Opening /hooks reloads the definitions.

targets.name: antigravity
targets.note: Antigravity and its CLI (agy) share hooks.json: ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json globally and .agents/hooks.json in a project, where hooks load only in a trusted folder. Each hook is a named block; Skillshare writes one block per hook, named after it. The CLI can also read hooks from ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, which Skillshare leaves untouched.

targets.name: pi
targets.note: Pi discovers extensions at startup; project extensions load only after project trust is granted. The code must use the extension API of your installed Pi version.

targets.name: omp
targets.note: Oh My Pi discovers extensions at startup from its agent directory (~/.omp/agent/extensions, or PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, which Pi reads too) and from .omp/extensions in a project. OMP has no project trust gate, so the next startup can execute the code. Its own hooks/pre and hooks/post factories are left untouched and listed as additional sources. The code must use the extension API of your installed OMP version.

targets.name: amp
targets.note: Amp runs plugins from its plugins folder with Bun; run 'plugins: reload' after sync. The code must use your Amp version's plugin API.

targets.name: opencode
targets.note: OpenCode loads plugins from its plugins folder. v1 plugins are named exports and v2 plugins export default Plugin.define(...); Skillshare writes your code as given and never converts between them.
